title: Solo Leveling
synopsis: Sung Jin-Woo, the weakest E-rank hunter, gains a unique system that lets him level up infinitely, transforming from prey into the most powerful hunter in the world.
review: An absolute page-turner. The progression system and escalating stakes make every arc feel earned. The art improves dramatically over time, reaching jaw-dropping levels in the final chapters.

title: Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood
synopsis: Two brothers search for the Philosopher's Stone to restore their bodies after a forbidden alchemy ritual goes wrong, uncovering a vast conspiracy along the way.
review: A masterclass in storytelling. Every plot thread is resolved, every character matters. The emotional payoff is unmatched in anime.

title: Berserk
synopsis: Guts, a lone mercenary with a tragic past, wages war against former friend Griffith and the godhand that cursed him, in a brutal dark fantasy world.
review: Miura's artwork is some of the finest ever put to page. The story is harrowing, beautiful, and deeply human despite its monstrous setting.

title: Attack on Titan
synopsis: Humanity lives behind walls to protect themselves from man-eating Titans, but the truth about the world is far more complex and devastating than anyone imagined.
review: Incredible plotting and foreshadowing. The way the mystery unfolds and the moral questions it raises in the final seasons elevate it beyond typical action anime.

title: The Beginning After The End
synopsis: A powerful king reincarnates into a magical world as a baby, retaining his memories. He navigates childhood while building toward an extraordinary new life.
review: Great world-building and character growth. The art is consistently gorgeous. The pacing dips in the middle but recovers strongly.

title: Vinland Saga
synopsis: A young Viking warrior named Thorfinn seeks revenge against the mercenary who killed his father, but his journey leads him to question the cycle of violence.
review: The character development from the Prologue to the Farmland arc is some of the best in manga. Thorfinn's transformation is profoundly moving.

title: Oshi no Ko
synopsis: A doctor and his patient are reincarnated as the twin children of a beloved idol, navigating the dark underbelly of the entertainment industry.
review: A brilliant blend of industry critique and supernatural mystery. The first arc is a perfect hook. The genre-switching keeps things fresh.

title: Demon Slayer
synopsis: Tanjiro Kamado becomes a demon slayer after his family is slaughtered and his sister turned into a demon, seeking a cure while battling powerful foes.
review: Ufotable's animation is simply the best in the industry. The story is straightforward but executed with incredible emotional resonance.

title: Tower of God
synopsis: A boy named Bam enters a mysterious tower to find his friend, climbing floors that test strength, intelligence, and willpower against other climbers.
review: Massive and creative world with deep lore. The early seasons are peak webtoon storytelling. The art starts rough but evolves beautifully.

title: Steins;Gate
synopsis: A self-proclaimed mad scientist accidentally discovers time travel, leading to a desperate struggle to save his friends from the consequences of altering the past.
review: Slow burn that pays off enormously. The second half is one of the most gripping narratives in anime. The emotional weight is crushing.

title: Jujutsu Kaisen
synopsis: Yuji Itadori swallows a cursed finger and joins a secret organization of jujutsu sorcerers to eliminate a powerful curse named Ryomen Sukuna.
review: Fantastic power system and some of the best fight choreography in manga. Gege's willingness to subvert expectations keeps you on edge.

title: Vagabond
synopsis: Based on the life of legendary swordsman Miyamoto Musashi, the story follows his journey from a brutal fighter to a man seeking the meaning of true strength.
review: Inoue's art is transcendent. Every panel is a painting. The philosophical depth elevates it beyond any battle manga.

title: Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint
synopsis: When the world transforms into the setting of a web novel only Kim Dokja read to completion, he uses his unique knowledge to survive and protect his companions.
review: One of the most clever narrative structures in manhwa. The meta-commentary on storytelling is brilliant, and the character bonds are deeply emotional.

title: Hunter x Hunter
synopsis: Gon Freecss sets out to become a Hunter and find his father, encountering friends, foes, and a deep power system along the way.
review: The nen system is the gold standard for power systems in anime. The Chimera Ant arc is one of the greatest storylines ever animated.

title: Made in Abyss
synopsis: A young girl and a robot boy descend into a vast, deadly abyss searching for her mother, facing terrifying creatures and the abyss's curse.
review: Beautiful art hiding a deeply unsettling story. The world-building is incredible and the emotional gut-punches never miss.

title: Wind Breaker
synopsis: A studious boy discovers a passion for cycling and joins a competitive team, finding friendship and purpose through the sport.
review: Surprisingly engaging sports manhwa with great character dynamics. The racing sequences are dynamic and exciting.

title: Chainsaw Man
synopsis: Denji, a young man burdened by debt, merges with his chainsaw devil dog Pochita and becomes a devil hunter for the government.
review: Fujimoto's unpredictable storytelling is refreshing. It's crude, hilarious, and surprisingly profound. The art is kinetic and visceral.

title: Mushishi
synopsis: Ginko travels across Japan studying mushi, ethereal creatures that exist between the natural and supernatural worlds, helping people affected by them.
review: A meditative, atmospheric masterpiece. Each episode is a self-contained story that lingers long after watching. The soundtrack is sublime.
